manifest.name: Filesystem
manifest.description: Let Claude access your filesystem to read and write files.
manifest.long_description:
This extension allows Claude to interact with your local filesystem, enabling it to read and write files directly. This can be useful for tasks such as file management, data processing, and automation of repetitive tasks. The extension provides a set of tools that can be used to navigate directories, read file contents, and write new files or modify existing ones.

Underneath the hood, it uses @modelcontextprotocol/server-filesystem.

tools.name: read_file
tools.description: Read the contents of a file

tools.name: read_multiple_files
tools.description: Read the contents of multiple files

tools.name: write_file
tools.description: Write content to a file

tools.name: edit_file
tools.description: Edit the contents of a file

tools.name: create_directory
tools.description: Create a new directory

tools.name: list_directory
tools.description: List contents of a directory

tools.name: directory_tree
tools.description: Display directory structure as a tree

tools.name: move_file
tools.description: Move or rename a file

tools.name: search_files
tools.description: Search for files by name or content

tools.name: get_file_info
tools.description: Get information about a file

tools.name: list_allowed_directories
tools.description: List directories that can be accessed

allowed_directories.title: Allowed Directories
allowed_directories.description: Select directories the filesystem server can access

manifest.name: Windows-MCP
manifest.description: MCP Server that enables Claude to interact with Windows OS
manifest.long_description:
Windows MCP is an open-source project that enables seamless integration between AI agents and the Windows operating system. Acting as an MCP server bridges the gap between LLMs and the Windows operating system, allowing agents to perform tasks such as **file navigation, application control, UI interaction, QA testing,** and more.

## Key Features

- **Seamless Windows Integration**: Interacts natively with Windows UI elements, opens apps, controls windows, simulates user input, and more.
- **Use Any LLM (Vision Optional)**: Unlike many automation tools, Windows MCP doesn't rely on any traditional computer vision techniques or specific fine-tuned models; it works with any LLMs, reducing complexity and setup time.
- **Rich Toolset for UI Automation**: Includes tools for basic keyboard, mouse operation and capturing window/UI state.
- **Lightweight & Open-Source**: Minimal dependencies and easy setup with full source code available under MIT license.
- **Customizable & Extendable**: Easily adapt or extend tools to suit your unique automation or AI integration needs.
- **Real-Time Interaction**: Typical latency between actions (e.g., from one mouse click to the next) ranges from **1.5 to 2.3 secs**, and may slightly vary based on the number of active applications and system load, also the inferencing speed of the llm.

## Requirements

### UV Package Manager
This MCP server requires [UV](https://github.com/astral-sh/uv), a fast Python package manager. 

```bash
pip install uv
```

For detailed installation instructions, see the [UV documentation](https://github.com/astral-sh/uv#installation).

tools.name: App Tool
tools.description: Manages Windows applications through launch, resize, and window switching operations.

tools.name: Powershell Tool
tools.description: Execute PowerShell commands and return the output with status code

tools.name: State Tool
tools.description: Capture comprehensive desktop state including focused/opened applications, interactive UI elements (buttons, text fields, menus), informative content (text, labels, status), and scrollable areas. Optionally includes visual screenshot when use_vision=True. Essential for understanding current desktop context and available UI interactions.

tools.name: Click Tool
tools.description: Click on UI elements at specific coordinates. Supports left/right/middle mouse buttons and single/double/triple clicks. Use coordinates from State Tool output.

tools.name: Type Tool
tools.description: Type text into input fields, text areas, or focused elements. Set clear=True to replace existing text, False to append. Click on target element coordinates first.

tools.name: Scroll Tool
tools.description: Scroll at specific coordinates or current mouse position. Use wheel_times to control scroll amount (1 wheel = ~3-5 lines). Essential for navigating lists, web pages, and long content.

tools.name: Drag Tool
tools.description: Drag and drop operation from source coordinates to destination coordinates. Useful for moving files, resizing windows, or drag-and-drop interactions.

tools.name: Move Tool
tools.description: Move mouse cursor to specific coordinates without clicking. Useful for hovering over elements or positioning cursor before other actions.

tools.name: Shortcut Tool
tools.description: Execute keyboard shortcuts using key combinations. Pass keys as list (e.g., 'ctrl'+'c' for copy, 'alt'+'tab' for app switching, 'win'+'r' for Run dialog, 'win' is for opening the start menu).

tools.name: Wait Tool
tools.description: Pause execution for specified duration in seconds. Useful for waiting for applications to load, animations to complete, or adding delays between actions.

tools.name: Scrape Tool
tools.description: Fetch and convert webpage content to markdown format. Provide full URL including protocol (http/https). Returns structured text content suitable for analysis.
